steps: An outside thread screws into an inside thread of the same size.
Note each rod's two ends and its length.
Chain rods so each joint pairs outside with inside; leave out any rod that cannot join.
The longest chain measures 1020.
qs.trap: Adding all the rods. Some ends cannot join, so not every rod fits the chain.

steps: Count row by row along the corridor.
A tile counts if any part of it is green.
Mark each counted tile lightly.
The total is 33.
qs.trap: Skipping tiles touched only at the patch edge.

steps: Faces parallel to the ground are the tops and bottoms of each die, including hidden ones.
Top and bottom of a die are opposite faces.
Use the net to find which faces are opposite on each die, given the visible faces.
Add the four top-bottom pairs: 27.
qs.trap: Counting only the visible top face. Hidden tops and bottoms are also parallel to the ground.

steps: Count upright squares of each size first: 1 × 1, 2 × 2 and so on.
Then count tilted squares, whose sides go diagonally across the grid.
Check that all four corners exist in the layout.
The total is 21.
qs.trap: Missing tilted squares.

steps: Black curved bits often fit into white curved gaps of the same radius.
Move each bulge into a matching dent.
The black area becomes simple rectangles or squares.
The area is 140 cm².
qs.trap: Working out each curved piece separately. Moving pieces is much faster.

steps: Each tile can be placed in 4 rotations.
The tile has no symmetry, so all 4 rotations look different.
Two tiles: 4 × 4 = 16 combinations.
All 16 patterns are different.
qs.trap: Dividing by 2 for swapping tiles. The two positions are different, so no swap removes duplicates.

steps: The plane passes through three corners next to one corner of the big cube, cutting it off.
Label small cubes by their distance from that corner.
Cubes one or two steps away are crossed by the plane: 3 + 6 = 9.
The corner cube only touches it; further cubes are not reached.

steps: Each new line can create triangles by crossing existing lines.
Place the lines so they cross every other line at a new point.
Count triangles of all sizes in the final figure.
The maximum is 10.
qs.trap: Placing lines through existing crossing points, which makes fewer triangles.

steps: Because rotations count as different, compare the angle of each motif too.
Sort motifs by shape, then by direction.
Tick each new one.
There are 8 distinct motifs.
qs.trap: Grouping a rotated motif with the original. Here, rotations count separately.

steps: Send the two fastest first: 2 minutes. The fastest brings the umbrella back: 1.
Now the two slowest go together: 10. The second fastest returns: 2.
The two fastest go again: 2.

steps: Turn every vowel: its back must be even.
Turn every odd number: its back must not be a vowel.
Consonants and even numbers cannot break the rule.
In this layout that means 3 cards.
qs.trap: Turning even numbers. An even number with a consonant behind it does not break the rule.

steps: Find how the operations turn X's edges into surfaces (for example, each edge becomes one side face, plus top and bottom).
Check the rule gives 14 for X.
Count Y's edges and apply the same rule.
Y gives 16 surfaces.
qs.trap: Guessing without testing the rule on X first.

steps: 2018 was not a leap year: 365 days × 24 = 8760 hours.
That is exactly one hour a day.

qs.trap: Using 366 days. 2018 was not a leap year.

steps: Count the grid squares and the squares in one tile.
The leftover must be at least the remainder when you divide.
Try to place tiles so only that remainder is left.
The fewest uncovered units is 4.
qs.trap: Assuming the remainder is always achievable. Check the shape can actually fit.

steps: A cut through the centre of a symmetric shape splits it into two equal halves.
The hole is placed so that two cuts through the centre, at right angles, give four equal parts.
Each part then has the same solid and the same share of the hole.
Two cuts are enough.
qs.trap: Answering 3, which you need only if the shape is not symmetric.

steps: Compare the pictures in a grid pattern.
Check colours, missing objects, positions and small details.
Mark each difference on both pictures.
There are 7 differences.
qs.trap: Scanning at random. A grid order finds all differences.

steps: Go line by line and mark where it meets or crosses another.
A point where three lines meet counts once.
Include ends where a line meets a curve.
The total is 44.
qs.trap: Counting a triple crossing as two or three intersections.

steps: Sort pineapples by their pattern: crown shape and skin texture.
Tally each type.
Find types that appear once.
Two types appear only once.
qs.trap: Treating a turned pineapple as a new type.

steps: Identify each disc's marks.
Rotate one disc over the other and see which combined images are possible.
Every mark in an option must come from one of the discs.
A and C can be made.
qs.trap: Accepting an image with a mark neither disc has.

steps: A: Turkle says children keep computers distinct from humans; they are not confused. False.
B: children learn to tell physical from psychological things by relating behaviour to nature. True.
C: the paragraph compares children with designers, not adults in general. False.
D: no such conclusion is made. False.
qs.trap: Choosing C because of the last sentence. It mentions the artefacts' designers, not all adults.

steps: Each copy can be turned to 4 positions.
Look for T-shapes in each option.
An option is possible if it splits into rotated Ts with nothing left over.
A, C and D can be made.
qs.trap: Accepting an image that needs a flipped T.

steps: Paths P›R and Q›T are diagonals; they cross where Puru meets Qadir.
Puru walks d + d. Qadir walks 0.62s + s + d. Both equal 3.24s, so A and B are false.
Roy walks R›T = d, exactly half of Qadir's distance: C is true.
Going home, Puru (T›P, a side) walks less than Qadir and Roy (diagonals): D is true.

steps: All shadows point the same way, because the light rays are parallel.
The cylinder's shadow is a long band with rounded ends; the cone's narrows to a point.
The sphere casts an ellipse starting under it.
A and C are correct.
qs.trap: Giving each shadow a different direction.

steps: Hands are at 90° 44 times a day, not 24: A false.
They overlap 22 times a day: B true.
They overlap exactly on a number marker only at 12: C true.
Over a day, acute and obtuse angles last about equally long: D true.

steps: With the Sun in the east, shadows point west.
One bug still faces north-east; the other now faces north.
Both shadows point west, whatever the bugs' direction.
B and D show this.
qs.trap: Turning the shadow with the bug. Shadows depend on the Sun, not the bug.

steps: The sharpener cuts a cone into the pentagonal body.
Where the cone meets the flat faces, the edges form curves.
From the side, curves appear on each visible face.
B and D show this.
qs.trap: Drawing straight edges where the cone meets the faces.

steps: Note how many half-twists the strip has.
A strip with one half-twist (Möbius) cut down the middle gives one longer loop.
Two half-twists give two linked loops.
C and D are the right results.
qs.trap: Expecting two separate loops whatever the twist.

steps: Put the clues in order: Monday < Friday < Wednesday and Thursday < Saturday < Sunday and Tuesday.
Wednesday and Thursday are not compared, so they could be equal: A true.
Tuesday and Sunday are not compared, so Tuesday could be longest: B true.
Monday is below everything: C true. Friday is shorter than Sunday: D false.

steps: The package has two triangular ends and three rectangular sides.
Check each net has three rectangles in a row and two triangles on opposite ends.
Make sure the triangles do not overlap when folded.
D cannot fold correctly.
qs.trap: Forgetting the question asks for CANNOT.

steps: Both pieces must fit in the figure at the same time, without overlapping.
Try placing each pair, rotating if needed.
If the second piece cannot fit in what is left, the pair fails.
B and D cannot be cut.
qs.trap: Checking each piece alone. Both pieces must fit together.

steps: A cup stacks if its base fits inside the rim of the cup below and rests on the walls.
Straight walls, wide bases or bulges stop it nesting.
Check each cup's shape.
A, B and C cannot stack; D can.
qs.trap: Choosing by looks. Check where the base touches the cup below.

steps: On a perfect circle, every copy is the same distance from the centre.
Check copies on opposite sides for equal distances.
Uneven gaps or distances show an oval.
C and D are not on a perfect circle.
qs.trap: Judging by overall roundness.

steps: Compare figure 1 with figures 2 and 3: what has been added?
Each option, flipped or rotated, must supply exactly those additions.
Check both figures for each option.
A, B and C work.
qs.trap: Checking only one of the two target figures.

steps: Q touches all 6 others, so Q is in the centre and the others form a ring.
In the ring each bee has two neighbours. P sits between T and V; U sits between R and S.
V does not touch T, U or R, so V's other neighbour must be S. That fixes the ring: T, P, V, S, U, R.
So S–V and R–T are neighbours, S–T are not: A, B and D. P and U are not neighbours.
qs.trap: Forgetting the queen takes the centre cell.

steps: Follow each string and note over and under crossings.
If the strings truly interlock, pulling tightens them into a knot.
If one string just lies on top, pulling separates them.
B and D form knots.
qs.trap: Counting crossings rather than following them.

qs.note: IIT Bombay gave full marks to all candidates because more than one solution was possible. Use it as practice: check which faces of the net would overlap its neighbours.

steps: Look for the rule across rows and down columns.
Test it on all rows.
Apply it to the gap.
A fits.
qs.trap: Using one row only.

steps: A slanted cut through a rolled tube becomes a wave when unrolled.
Two slanted cuts make two waves.
The middle part lies between the two waves.
C shows this.
qs.trap: Expecting straight slanted edges. Cuts across a roll unroll into curves.

steps: Compare stroke contrast, serifs and the shapes of letters like a, g and e.
Ignore size and colour.
Find the option matching every feature.
D matches.
qs.trap: Choosing by weight or size.

steps: Still water reflects things upside down, directly below.
The reflection shows the underside of the boat, as seen from water level.
It is the same width, directly under the boat.
B is correct.
qs.trap: Simply flipping the picture. A reflection shows the view from below.

steps: The ant's eye is almost at table level.
Objects look tall and big; we see their undersides and edges.
Check which way the glasses face from the ant's position.
A shows the ant's view.
qs.trap: Choosing a top view. The ant looks along the table.

steps: "glitive" is in both woodboard and foodwood, so glitive = wood.
So the code reverses word order: drasso glitive = board wood.
Then dresso = screen (from digitalscreen, reversed).
"screensize" reversed is size + screen: issics + dresso = issicsdresso.

qs.trap: Keeping the English word order. The code puts the second word first.

steps: The cylinder turns steadily, so time runs along the unrolled paper.
While the pencil moves, the line slopes; while it stops, the line is flat.
The slope depends on how fast the pencil moves in each part.
A shows: slope, flat, gentler slope.
qs.trap: Forgetting the pause, which shows as a flat part.

steps: The disc is parallel to the table.
Parallel light projects a flat shape onto a parallel surface without distorting it.
So the shadow is a circle of the same size, just shifted.
C shows a circle.
qs.trap: Expecting an ellipse. Only a tilted disc casts an ellipse on a level table.

steps: A knight moves in an L: two squares one way, one square sideways.
Mark squares the knight can reach in 1 move, then 2, and so on.
Skip squares with pawns.
The opposite corner is first reached in 6 moves.
qs.trap: Ignoring blocked squares.

steps: Identify each piece.
Try to build each option without flipping.
One option needs a flipped piece.
D is not possible.
qs.trap: Flipping a piece in your head.

steps: A point light makes shadows grow with distance from the lamp.
Light passes through the cut-outs and makes bright shapes in the shadow.
Shapes near the bottom of the card appear nearer the card.
C shows the correct enlarged shadow.
qs.trap: Treating the lamp like the Sun. A nearby lamp enlarges the shadow.

steps: Find the rule shared by three of the items.
Check each item against the rule.
One breaks it.
B is the odd one.
qs.trap: Choosing on looks alone.

steps: A heavy box in front pulls the body forward.
To balance, he leans back and plants his feet wider and slightly forward.
His centre of weight must stay over his feet.
C shows this.
qs.trap: Choosing a straight upright stance. A heavy load needs a lean.

steps: Count faces and their shapes.
Match faces that touch in the views with faces that join in the net.
Fold in your mind.
B works.
qs.trap: Checking face count only.

steps: A squeegee drags paint in the direction it moves.
Splatters become streaks, thick where there was more paint.
The streaks start at the splatter and fade along the pull.
D shows this.
qs.trap: Streaking in the wrong direction.

steps: It works like a sudoku with colours.
Fill the cells with only one possible colour first.
Use rows, columns and compartments together.
C fills the gaps.
qs.trap: Checking only the row.

steps: A giant's eyes are high, so it looks down on the buildings.
Rooftops are visible and buildings narrow towards the ground.
Streets look small.
C shows this.
qs.trap: Choosing a street-level view.

steps: The chain of hexagons is the same shape in every frame, only turned.
The pink and teal dots move along the chain from frame to frame.
Continue both changes one more step: the turn and the dot movement.
The official key gives B.
qs.trap: Checking only the shape. The dot positions decide between options.

steps: Follow the disc through a full turn and mark X's position at several points.
Join the marks.
Check the shape against the options.
D is the path.
qs.trap: Guessing a circle. Linked bars usually trace odd shapes.

steps: Light comes from the strike's position.
Bright faces point towards it; shadows fall away from it.
Check every object.
A is correct.
qs.trap: Choosing a scene lit from a different direction.

steps: Use the scale bar under each map.
Compare each lake to the same scale, not by its picture size.
Estimate area roughly.
D is the largest.
qs.trap: Comparing picture sizes. Each map has its own scale.

steps: Find one distinctive feature in each tile.
Look for it repeated in each pattern.
Match all four, checking rotations.
qs.trap: Matching by colour alone.

steps: Compare outlines, including gaps between parts.
Check small details: handles, edges, spaces.
Find the option where all match.
B matches.
qs.trap: Checking only the overall shape.

steps: Each ring turns as it rolls; distance rolled = angle turned × radius.
Track a mark on each ring to see how far it turns.
Place all three centred on XX'.
B shows the result.
qs.trap: Forgetting that rolling also turns the ring.

steps: Lowering means the line moves down on the clothes side.
Follow the line over each pulley to see which way it must turn.
All pulleys must agree with the line's motion.
C is right.
qs.trap: Turning all pulleys the same way. The line wraps differently on each.

steps: The colours move round the colour wheel in small steps: green, cyan, blue, navy, violet, magenta, red, red-orange.
Each step is about the same small change in hue.
After red-orange comes orange.
A is orange: A.
qs.trap: Jumping to yellow. The steps are small, so the next colour is only a little different.

steps: Odd letters (A, C, E, G...) are upper case; even letters (b, d, f, h...) are lower case.
H (8th) and L (12th) and P (16th) are lower case, turned anticlockwise.
E (5th) is upper case, turned clockwise.
Option A shows h, E, l, p turned correctly.
qs.trap: Writing every letter in capitals.

qs.note: IIT Bombay gave full marks to all candidates because more than one solution was possible.
IIT Bombay gave full marks to all candidates because more than one solution was possible. As practice, try fitting the pieces into a square.

steps: Find the rule across the figure.
Test it on every part.
Apply it to the gap.
B fits.
qs.trap: Using one part only.

steps: Look for what all the objects have in common: use, material or action.
Test each option against every object.
One option links them all.
C is correct.
qs.trap: Choosing a link that fits most but not all objects.

steps: Compare the options carefully with the given figure.
Look for the one small difference.
Eliminate options that break the pattern.
A is correct.
qs.trap: Rushing a question that looks simple.
